headline: Karpathy's weekend toy grew into a whole series in a day
summary: HN is flooded with HackerTube spinoffs; also one company run almost entirely by agents that's worth knowing about.

items.title: HackerBooks: the books HN keeps recommending
items.pitch: Same trick, different target: dig up the books that keep coming up across 20 years of HN threads and turn them into a site. Free, no login—perfect for a weekend browse.
why: The list comes from real comments, not a ranking gamed by votes
Wikihack and HackerHack popped up in the same wave
Opens on mobile, no signup, zero barrier
actions: If you want to find stuff by wiki entry, try wikihack.netlify.app
deep_dive: Unlike Douban or Goodreads, it doesn't give ratings—it just counts the books that keep getting mentioned in HN comments.
Pure web page, static index, loads fast; basically turns 'what HN has mentioned' into a searchable catalog.
Limitation: it skews toward the English tech crowd; new books and Chinese books are basically missing, so don't expect it to work as a mainstream book list.
items.signals: HN 1479 points · 246 comments · 20 hours · same wave Wikihack 242 points

items.title: Spawn: a company run almost entirely by agents
items.pitch: A company burns $3M a month in tokens letting agents change code, fix bugs, and ship every hour. Simon Willison tried it himself—says it's crazy but it really runs.
why: 60% of the work starts automatically from online errors
If nothing ships in an hour, it's treated as a top-severity outage
A preview of what 'everyone managing a fleet of agents' looks like
items.signals: Simon Willison hands-on · $3M/month in tokens · deploys hourly
